🦈 Welcome Aboard!

Exploring South Florida's Sharks & Red Tide

Hi there! This website investigates how coastal sharks around Miami and the Florida Keys respond to Karenia brevis harmful algal blooms (red tide). Use this illustrated guide to swim through each tab of our project and see how marine survey data, maps, and statistics come together!

🌊 The Big Question We're Investigating

Along Southwest Florida's Gulf coast, microscopic algae called Karenia brevis bloom nearly every year, releasing neurotoxins and depleting oxygen in coastal waters. Meanwhile, South Florida's Atlantic coast around Miami and Biscayne Bay is usually sheltered—until rare ocean current events (like in 2018) carry red tide right around the Florida Keys!

By combining 13 years of University of Miami shark drumline surveys with Florida FWC & NOAA red tide water monitoring, this website explores how sharks move between coasts and how their catch rates change during bloom years.
